title.narrative: Decarbonisation and sustainable cities for a net-zero future in Malaysia

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project is designed to deliver various environmental and socio-economic benefits, contributing to local development objectives and broader national and global sustainability targets. Key anticipated socio-economic impacts include: - Improved urban liveability and quality of life: By embedding sustainability principles into urban development planning and implementation, the project will contribute to healthier, safer, and more inclusive urban environments. Greener cities, featuring improved air quality, public transport, green spaces, and reduced pollution, will enhance the overall well-being of residents. - Reduced energy-related emissions and energy costs: The project will reduce dependency on fossil fuels, lower urban emissions, and generate cost savings for municipal authorities, businesses, and households over time by deploying renewable energy technologies and energy efficiency measures. - Increased urban resilience to climate impacts: Strategic planning and infrastructure upgrades will enhance cities' capacity to withstand and recover from extreme weather events, particularly urban flooding, safeguarding communities, assets, and local economies. - Enabling environment for sustainable investment: The project will help cities become more investment-ready by demonstrating viable business models, integrating climate considerations into procurement and planning, and improving policy coherence. This will strengthen their ability to mobilize public and private financing for future sustainability-related infrastructure and services. - Strengthened knowledge base and institutional capacity: The project will foster long-term institutional learning through peer exchange, training, and knowledge sharing. This will generate replicable tools and experiences to inform future projects in Malaysia and other GEF partner countries. - Green job creation and economic development: The project will stimulate the local green economy by designing, installing, and maintaining low-carbon and nature-based infrastructure. This is expected to generate employment opportunities and support the development of local expertise and green SMEs.

The projectâ€™s objective is to catalyze urban decarbonization in Selangor as a strategic entry point for addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, and land degradation, by integrating innovative policies, technologies, and financing mechanisms into city planning and investment frameworks, creating scalable models for sustainable, resilient, and inclusive urban development in Malaysia.
